name: Jessie Doe Hall
use: Residence hall, 129 students, first-year and upper-division
architect: Maurice E. Witmer, AIA (contractor Bond Bros., Inc.)

facts.text: Opened in September 1963 as a women's residence and dedicated May 9, 1964; designed by Maurice E. Witmer, AIA, and built by Bond Bros.
Named for Jessie Doe (1887–1943), the first woman to serve in the New Hampshire legislature and a UNH trustee 1934–1943.
Small hall of 129 students at 24 Ballard Street, next to the Whittemore Center, with a basement study lounge and a first-floor lounge with pool, ping-pong, fireplace and big-screen TV.
Accessibility listed as braille signage and roll-in building access; no elevator or A/C listed.

verdict: Plain 1963 brick dorm by the Whittemore Center, named for New Hampshire's first woman legislator; tight-knit but tired.
notes: No interior renovation found; the old row's 2023 utility pipe work and TNH vandalism story were not re-verified. Photos: plain four-storey red-brick slab with low-pitched roof, a glazed stair tower over a flat-canopied entry, set among pines; fireplace lounge has dropped acoustic-tile ceiling, painted block walls and fluorescent lighting, with windows on one side. Housing page shows the hall as first-year and upper-division (old row said first-year). No licensed photo found (searched the Commons category tree under 'University of New Hampshire' and 'Durham, New Hampshire', Commons file search by name, Commons geosearch at the building's coordinates, and Openverse/Flickr CC).
judgeNotes: Reference photos: four-storey brick slab, dated block-walled lounge.
